leading_positions.synthesis: Four members prefer optical lattice clocks (Katori, Ye) as a single-achievement prize. They share the view that the magic-wavelength lattice is a distinct invention from ion clocks, that the 1e-18 level has been reproduced and intercompared across laboratories, and that the two-name credit is the cleanest on the list. They differ in how they word the citation (Johansson and Kroll want it tied to the magic-wavelength lattice, Pearce wants it about the invention and demonstrated accuracy rather than the pending redefinition of the second), in how openly to acknowledge Paris and other contributors, and in how much weight to give theory (Kroll) versus experiment. All four list the overlap with the 1997, 2005 and 2012 prizes as the main risk, and none of them has checked the priority history from primary sources. Two (Kroll, Lindroth) ranked it first in the opening round; Johansson changed her preferred configuration to it in round 1.

Three members prefer the topological-insulator entry with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp (prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, plus the HgTe observation). All three moved to B042 from other opening favourites (B018, B005, B012), and all name B037 as an alternative or a fallback. They share the view that the field is mature and the prediction-then-measurement chain is clear. They differ on Xue's quantum anomalous Hall work: Olsson regrets losing it as a separate experimental discovery, Mehlig prefers the narrower framing. All three concede that the omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (Zhang deceased), the 3D work (Fu, Moore, Balents, Hasan) and the 2016 topology prize are real weaknesses, and want a citation that does not claim the whole story.

One member prefers the ATLAS and CMS Higgs discovery (Della Negra, Jenni, Virdee), as the unrecognised experimental half of a discovery whose theory was honoured in 2013, with a mature and stable interpretation. He states openly that the three-name leadership credit is a compromise and that, if the committee cannot defend it, B037 is the better choice; B037 and B003 are his alternatives. Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce each questioned the leadership attribution in their responses; Eriksson deferred on the physics but shared the attribution worry.

areas_of_agreement: No member's preferred configuration is a two-part prize; all eight prefer a single ballot ID, and Johansson, Eriksson and Olsson wrote that B042 and B012 describe one field and must not be stacked.

B037, the optical lattice clock, is the entry most widely supported in the files: Johansson reports that none of the seven members who ranked it raised a scientific objection, and Danielsson, Eriksson, Mehlig and Olsson each name it as an alternative or say they would not block it.

Members who comment on the physics agree that B042 and B037 are mature, reproduced and stably interpreted, and that B018 (twisted bilayer graphene) is less mature because the origin of the correlated phases and superconductivity is unsettled.
Several members (Mehlig, Eriksson, Olsson, Johansson) say B042 must be separated from B012 and use one framing.

Several members (Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson, Pearce) see the 2025 superconducting-circuit prize as a reason for caution on circuit QED (B008), although Olsson and Pearce add that this is a timing argument, not a merit argument.

Members from several fields (Lindroth, Kroll, Mehlig, Pearce) ask that the priority history behind the B037 and B042 credits be checked against primary papers or an expert report before a final ballot.
scientific_disputes: Whether the optical lattice clock is a distinct new regime (many neutral atoms interrogated at a magic wavelength, a many-body regime of clock physics) or an evolutionary refinement of the frequency comb (2005) and ion-control (2012) prizes. Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth and Pearce argue the former; the same four list the overlap as the main risk.

Whether a lattice clock is a discovery about nature or a measurement method. Danielsson says the Higgs result is a discovery of what the world is made of, while Kroll and Pearce answer that the clock is an instrument with measured and published figures of merit. Kroll notes no new physics has yet been seen with the clocks.

Whether the 2016 prize for topological phases of matter leaves room for B042. Eriksson, Mehlig and Olsson argue that time-reversal-invariant Z2 insulators are distinct from the quantum Hall and Haldane lineage; Johansson and Mehlig record that some colleagues feel the area is saturated.

Whether B018 is mature enough: Eriksson accepts that the superconducting mechanism is unsettled, Mehlig, Danielsson, Johansson and Pearce weigh that more heavily, and Eriksson no longer holds it as a first choice.
Whether B005 (active matter) can be tested well enough: Mehlig concedes the precise exponents are only partly tested and that it cannot currently gain support beyond his own ranking.
attribution_disputes: B006: the three names are founding spokespersons and project leaders of ATLAS and CMS. Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce question whether leadership is the decisive contribution under the statute, and Olsson notes the spokespersons at the time of discovery were different people. Danielsson himself calls it a compromise.

B042: the credit omits Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (whose HgTe proposal guided Molenkamp, with Zhang deceased), Fu, Moore, Balents and Hasan on the 3D case. B012 swaps Mele for Xue, and so credits the quantum anomalous Hall experiment instead of Mele. Eriksson, Mehlig and Olsson accept B042 with a carefully worded citation; Kroll says he would need a convincing answer on BHZ before ranking it above B037.

B037: the two names are agreed in every ballot that ranked it, but Lemonde and the Paris group, Boulder and NIST contributors and the ion-clock community also have claims; Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth and Pearce say this should be acknowledged openly. Lindroth, Johansson and Kroll oppose widening the citation to ion clocks. The magic-wavelength priority history is recalled from memory by Lindroth and unverified by Kroll and Mehlig.

B003 (Pearce's opening first choice, now an alternative to B037): the split between the BeppoSAX team and ground-based follow-up is debatable, van Paradijs's optical identification is outside the three names and one important contributor is deceased.
B008: Girvin and Huang co-authored the circuit QED proposal and are not among the credited names (raised by Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson, Pearce).
maturity_disputes: B037: the redefinition of the second has not happened, and geodesy and constant-variation tests are partly prospective. Kroll, Pearce and Johansson say the redefinition argues for timeliness but should not drive the citation.
B018: the origin of the correlated phases and superconductivity is debated, and several members would wait (Eriksson, Mehlig, Danielsson, Johansson).
B042: the field has had about fifteen years to consolidate and is called mature by its supporters; the dispute is about overlap and credit, not maturity.
B006: the Higgs interpretation has been stable for a decade, as Danielsson and Eriksson say; maturity is not in dispute, only credit.
B005: only partial experimental tests of the precise exponents (Mehlig, Danielsson).
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson (B008): director of WACQT at Chalmers and close to the circuit-QED community, who ranked B008 first in the opening round; she says she would recuse herself from the final decision on B008 if it advanced and asks that her views on it be treated with caution.

Kroll (B037): spent a year in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder, and says Jun Ye is a scientific descendant of that JILA environment; he has no personal or financial tie to Ye or Katori but states that a recusal question could be raised. He also flags that his role at the Chalmers-led Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology overlaps institutionally with Johansson and with the field behind B008, and says he should not decide on circuit QED.

Lindroth (B037 field): a long-time collaborator of Anne L'Huillier and the Lund attosecond groups, working in the same broad atomic, molecular and optical community as the clock groups; she says none of these links involves a shortlisted candidate and has a familiarity caveat.

Pearce (B003, B006; chair): general field affinity to high-energy astrophysics and Fermi-LAT, and a CERN PhD background, with no personal or institutional tie to the credited names for B003 or to ATLAS or CMS. He is an astroparticle physicist and cannot settle the atomic-physics relative-merit question himself.
Eriksson (B042, B018): his field of first-principles electronic structure is close in subject to B042 and B018, but he states this is expertise, not a personal tie.
Mehlig, Olsson: note only that Johansson, Mehlig and Olsson are in the Gothenburg (Chalmers) physics environment, with no specific collaboration found; Mehlig says no recusal is needed.
Danielsson: no conflict apparent; his ties to David Gross and the Uppsala string group do not touch shortlisted candidates.
questions_for_round2: For B037: can the atomic-physics members (Lindroth, Johansson, Kroll) set out, from the primary papers, the separable priority of Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and first strontium lattice clock against Ye's accuracy and many-body work and the contemporaneous Paris and Boulder groups, and state whether two names are sufficient?

For B037: what exactly is new relative to the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize, and can the citation say so in terms of the magic-wavelength lattice and ensemble interrogation without pointing to the redefinition of the second?

For B042: can a citation be drafted for Kane, Mele and Molenkamp that honours the Z2 prediction and the HgTe observation without implying that Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, the 3D materials work or the quantum anomalous Hall effect are attributed to them, and is that wording acceptable to Kroll and Danielsson, who have raised the BHZ and attribution concerns?

For B042: does the 2016 topological-phases prize leave room, and can Eriksson, Mehlig and Olsson state what distinguishes time-reversal-invariant Z2 insulators from the Thouless, Haldane and Kosterlitz lineage in terms the other members can assess?

For B006: is there a defensible rationale for crediting Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee for conception and leadership, and would Danielsson accept B037 as a fallback if the committee finds that none exists; and can the members who rank it, or Pearce as a particle physicist, say who the decisive contributors were at the time of discovery?

Would the members who prefer B037 and B042 each say how they would order the other, since B037 is named as an alternative by Danielsson, Eriksson, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce and B042 by Lindroth, Kroll, Johansson and Pearce, and what would change their ordering?

For B008 and B018: is there any member who would now put either in a preferred configuration, given the 2025 superconducting-circuit prize, the Girvin and Huang omission and the unsettled correlated phases, or should round 2 set both aside?
summary.chair_observation: On the explicit round-1 positions, eight members split four (B037), three (B042) and one (B006) between single-achievement prizes, with no preferred configuration containing more than one ballot ID. B037 is the most frequently named alternative as well, but its supporters and the B042 supporters each say the other would be an acceptable fallback; I am not counting hidden votes. The open items are evidence checks (priority history for B037 and the BHZ omission for B042), the overlap with earlier prizes, and whether the three-name B006 leadership credit can be defended. Round 2 should address those before any ordering.
